Is anyone answering these phones?
Can you hear me?
How thin is the skin between realms?
How strong is the connection?
Don't hang up. 
Who's calling?
Is the great beyond really so far away?
Is the unknown merely unanswered?
Does the otherside surround us?
I was just about to call you. 
In the great sleep, is there conversation?
In the silent rigor, is there dialogue?
Can I take a message?
I'll tell them you called. 
One moment. 
I've been trying to reach you. 
It's been forever, I thought I lost you. 
And if it were so - would you pick up the phone?
What would you say?
...are you still there?

name: Golden Ladder
subtitle: Mantis
hometown: Santa Cruz, CA; Cologne, Germany; Katowice, Poland; Cuneo, Italy
description:
The Golden Ladder - Getting people high since 6.000 BC.
Each step will take you higher, your perspective shifts, your fear goes. The EXIT is close. Turn around and see from where you came. Curious minds, standing high, you don't need to touch the stars, yet realize, every one of us is a star. Leave with freshly earned gains.

name: The Paradox Post
subtitle: Daniel Taylor & Sucre Rosa
description: Paradox Post is a kinetic signpost that playfully satirizes human confirmation bias. Built from scavenged materials and recycled community paint, the installation features four stacked, rotating wooden signs. Each side of the manually rotating signs displays perfectly contradictory advice, such as "Speak your truth" and "Silence is golden." The piece serves as a humorous oracle of convenient truth. Participants physically spin the signs until they align the exact combination of profound-sounding wisdom required to justify whatever decisions they already want to make.

name: Tandem
subtitle: David & Jenni
description: It looks like a tandem bicycle, weeeeeeee!

name: Moi
subtitle: Kayfab
description: Moi is a 3ft metal divine swine sculpture.  She has learned to love herself and therefore can share that with the world, which makes her the ultimate fabulous version of all swine.

name: Playback
subtitle: Open Dreamers
description: Playback creates a bridge back into yourself, at a time where everything around you is pulling you outwards, an analog connection with your inner realm is often the most precious and human thing that you have left.

name: Back In 30 Minutes
subtitle: Iron Monkeys
description: The Iron Monkeys are shifting focus from the monumental to the miniature. This year, we've forged a large steel frame of our logo and filled it entirely with a dense collage of smaller, individual art pieces. It's a reminder that even when the heavy machinery rests and the crew steps away, idle hands keep on creating. Look closely, and don't mind the sign.

name: Spots
subtitle: The Serendipsters
description:
Spots is a collection of oversized map pins appearing individually across Black Rock City, each eight feet tall, black and bold, outlined in reflective yellow tape. A six-foot flag pole rises above each pin, its label lit by solar lights at night. Every pin swivels so it can be read from any direction.

Each pin marks a specific kind of human moment: The Hugging Spot, The Giggling Spot, with more arriving in future years. They borrow the visual language of digital navigation and plant it in the most radically human place on earth, marking locations found on no map app.
Spots asks nothing. It simply identifies what is already possible anywhere two strangers stand near each other, unhurried, present, closer to something real than expected.

name: BLACK ROCK ADVENTURES BUS STOP!
subtitle: Black Rock Adventures & Ironsides Design
hometown: Los Angeles CA / Billings MT / Portland OR
description: This not only looks like a bus stop, it is a BUS STOP! Playa Tours depart from the BUS STOP! Daily at 9am in our accessible adventure rig....come for a tour with us!

name: Soul Tree
subtitle: Astro  (Kenny Sokolowski)
description: Soul Tree is an illuminated life size wire tree. It is a metaphor for life choices and free will, each strand being a thought or choice in ones life, the intertwined wires are self strengthening choices and actions, making branches that define a focus of our souls intention. Just as one can easily manipulate the direction of the Soul Trees wires and branches, one can manipulate their soul's trajectory through this life. No matter the past forces or decisions one has experienced, there is always room for redirection and restructuring. There is not one perfect Soul Tree but an infinite variety, everyone has the ability to keep growing and changing their trajectory. The only constant is change.

name: I Have Dust In Curious Places
subtitle: Scott Copernicus
hometown: Another Place, Another Time, NV, United States
description: It's a cheeky sign.

name: Conduit
subtitle: Josh Epperson
description: Conduit is an immersive light sculpture exploring the invisible pathways that connect people, ideas, energy, and community. A 11-foot by 13-foot steel structure incorporates laser-cut stainless steel infinity mirror panels illuminated by programmable LED lighting. During the day, layered geometric patterns create transparency and shifting views through the structure. At night, mirrored panels and internal lighting create the illusion of depth extending beyond the physical boundaries of the artwork. Inspired by sacred geometry, networks, and waveforms, Conduit reflects the belief that meaningful connections illuminate human experience and transform individual elements into something greater.

name: The Last Shore
subtitle: Otabek Suleymanov, Stihia Festival
description:
The Last Shore is an interactive portal inspired by the disappearance of the Aral Sea, once the fourth-largest inland lake on Earth.
A freestanding frame filled with suspended reflective elements and transparent droplets creates the illusion of shimmering water suspended in space. As participants pass through the portal, a hidden soundscape evokes waves, wind, seabirds, and voices from the Aral Sea region.
Created by Stihia community from Muynak, a former fishing town on the Aral Sea, the work explores memory, loss, and transformation. It creates a symbolic connection between two former seabeds: the Aral Sea and Black Rock Desert, inviting reflection on what remains after landscapes change.

name: Above the Noise
subtitle: Jason Olsen
hometown: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: A monumental 13-foot-tall piano bench rises unexpectedly from the open playa, supporting a functioning full size grand piano high above the desert floor. Familiar in form yet impossible in scale, the installation transforms an ordinary object into something surreal, evoking wonder, vulnerability, and perspective. By day, it appears stark against the vastness of Black Rock Desert; by night, LED lighting outlines the structure and softly illuminates the piano above. The work reflects on elevation, both physical and emotional, and the role music plays in grounding, connection, reflection, and shared human experience.

name: Tengri Oasis
subtitle: Tengri Camp
description: Tengri Oasis is represented by a monumental reclining camel inspired by the nomadic cultures of Central Asia. Its three humps are formed by the exposed wooden frameworks of traditional yurts, transformed into transparent sculptural elements that reveal the geometry and craftsmanship of nomadic architecture. Three Altybaqan swings stand beside the camel, referencing a traditional space for gathering, storytelling, and celebration. Rooted in the values of freedom, hospitality, and connection to nature, the installation reimagines the ancient nomadic journey as an Axis Mundi—a symbolic link between earth and sky, movement and stillness, individual experience and collective belonging.

name: Larrys Hat
subtitle: The Office of Permits and Regulations
description:
"The Hat" is a site-specific installation consisting of a hat suspended above a simple illuminated platform on the Black Rock Desert. At night, lighting creates a defined square of attention within the vast openness of the playa, inviting participants to approach, gather, and linger. This well-traveled installation – appearing previously on the playa every year since Larry Harvey's death as well as the BLM Field Office in Winnemucca - is a precisely cited installation that evokes and perpetuates the playa rumor that Larry Harvey was buried within the Black Rock Desert, and this installation marks the spot. The work encourages visitors to create their own narratives, share stories, and debate its meaning.
40°44'45.2"N 119°10'24.0"W

name: Christo at the Trash Fence, or, Curtains for Black Rock City
subtitle: Just John
description:
Salvaged fabric from Christo's famous 1976 landscape art, the 24.5-mile-long "Running Fence" used for curtains to beautify the trash fence.

The Running Fence was originally conceived as "Curtains for West Berlin," a project to cover the infamous Berlin Wall that separated the democratic West from authoritarian East Berlin. Black Rock City has a similar structure blocking citizens from entering federal land. 

Christo cancelled his long-planned "Over The River" project in 2017 after the surprise outcome of the federal election saying: "I can't do a project that benefits this landlord."

We will never see "Over The River," but since we are already permitted, we will implement the concept of "Curtains" at Black Rock City."

name: We Hold These Truths: E Pluribus Playa
subtitle: Smithsonian Folklife Festival
description: This mobile community recording activity moves through Black Rock City, showing up at camps, events, on the open playa, and by the ARTery. The title comes from one of the most recognizable lines in the Declaration of Independence, which marks its 250th anniversary in 2026. This project records short conversations about gathering, community, history, and shared futures in this unique moment and place. Grounded in exchange and collective reflection, it contributes to an evolving record documented by the Smithsonian, exploring the truths communities negotiate and share, while affirming citizenship as a practice of participation, responsibility, and care.

name: The Only Way Out Is In
subtitle: Richard Card
hometown: Dallas and Austin, TX; Joshua Tree, CA
description:
A tunnel of seven nested rainbow arches with a circular mirror at its center. Crystal prisms hang from each arch, scattering light across the playa. Seven questions of self-reflection are mounted inside, asking visitors to look
inward and consider their past year, its storms and its rainbows. At night, the LED-lit arches glow across the open playa. It is a meditation on transition: a reminder that every storm passes, and that it is our strife that makes the rainbow possible.

name: Chroma Commons at the ARTery
subtitle: Dusty Nation, Lead Artist Cameron Anne Mason
description: In a temporary city in a constant state of metamorphosis, Chroma Commons creates a sense of place using ephemeral materials: Silk, color, and air. Simple yet dramatic, this moving color field activates the ARTery. Look closer and the silks reveal subtle texture and hues gradating along the color wheel. The slightest breeze creates a kinetic environment and provides changing views.

name: Aunisoma
subtitle: Dave Clay
description: Our perception of reality is colored not only by our own emotions but through others and by the external world. How we understand something at one moment may not be the same in the next moment. We all live together in a multi-colored world that is often out of our control. This piece aims to embrace all that beautiful chaos of all these beautiful people into something to be celebrated, allowing ourselves to be curious, explore, and adapt to the ever-changing internal and external realities.

name: Moroccan ParTea
subtitle: Hind Baghdadi
description:
My installation art is to honor my fellow Moroccans and Moroccan hospitality; to honor their generosity and their beautiful hearts. 
A Moroccan citizen welcomes everyone with open arms and open hearts no matter their age, gender, religion, race, color - none of that matters, a mint tea is always offered from the heart and with pure love.

name: Earth Guardians of Cryptometria Tree
subtitle: Leyla Brashka
description:
The installation consists of two nature beings that are the guardians of Cryptomeria tree.
One is a flower being with leaves and the other one is a mushroom being, both connected by mycelium through their feet between each other and the Cryptometria tree, honoring the underground network of connection that facilitates communication and resource sharing between trees, plants and mushrooms, manifesting the intrinsic connection trees have within themselves and the mushrooms and plants having all together synergy between them. Being used as a metaphor as well to manifest the intrinsic connection we have with Mother Earth and between each other as living beings through an invisible thread.

name: Still Point, or "At the still point of the turning world."
subtitle: Imogen Speer
description: Still Point traces the correspondence between macrocosm and microcosm, revealing patterns that recur throughout life and the value we ascribe them. The installation consists of two mixed-media panels, each approximately 12 by 8–10 feet, combining painting, collage, and gold leaf. One panel contains enlarged animal, bacterial, and plant cells, where cycles of birth, growth, movement, and dissolution unfold alongside fragments of human experience. The other presents an angelic figure juxtaposed against the solar system, her form divided into scenes of memory, value, and meaning-making. Together, the works contemplate scale and intimacy, transience and continuity, the reflective still point of conscious existence.

name: Resonance
subtitle: Raylene Gorum
description: Resonance is a suspended pendant of forty layered panels whose shifting linework evokes ripples, tree rings, and waves of sound. Derived from the geometry of Black Rock City, the layered forms transform the city's familiar plan into a visible record of time as it approaches its 40th Burn. As participants move through the Man, the layers align and separate, revealing changing relationships between the vibrating patterns and framed views beyond. Looking back toward the city through the pendant's center, past and present briefly converge. Suspended beneath Cryptomeria, the work reflects the theme of Axis Mundi by connecting forty years of collective creation through the continual making and remaking of Black Rock City.

name: I am the Light. I remember
subtitle: STuro
description: "I am the Light. I remember" depicts ancient guardians as living expressions of memory, consciousness, and humanity's enduring relationship with nature. It celebrates the Axis Mundi - the world tree that unites earth, sky, and unseen realms. Here, the Cryptomeria becomes more than a tree; it becomes a universal symbol and interconnected life. The title "I am the Light. I Remember" expresses a journey inward. It invites burners to remember their shared humanity and their relationship with their own soul. As burners and participants pass between the Guardians of Cryptomeria into the heart of the trunk, they symbolically leave behind separation and enter a sanctuary of contemplation, where art and community converge in the spirit of Burning Man.

name: Emergence
subtitle: Julia Jerome
description:
Inside a sealed case hangs a sheet of translucent material. It flows like fabric though it is solid, glows like amber, and catches light like glass.

It is skin.

Made by dissolving animal hide and allowing it to dry, the material reorganizes itself in response to heat, humidity, gravity, and the presence of other objects in its environment.

Emergence draws on the idea that complex patterns arise from countless simple interactions. Just as collagen molecules become skin, and nebulas give birth to stars, this material forms something entirely new. Everything is a temporary arrangement of matter, continually dissolving and becoming. What will your matter become next?

name: Scared Sacred
subtitle: Dust and Beau
description: Scared Sacred is a play on the balance between light and darkness. The lower half features a trunk that is entwined with serpent creatures and tentacles. The upper branches are adorned with backlit crystals and crystal chandeliers that emit a warm glow, creating a striking contrast with the darkness below. The intentional interplay between the trunk and the canopy emphasizes the balance between light and dark.

name: ELEMENTALS
subtitle: Chelsey Hathman & Sterling Fortaliza
description: The elementals are tree spirits that help guide your messages to the cosmos. Each element, water, fire, earth, and wind, is an ancient entity that will ask something of you. Water asks: What wants to flow for you? Fire asks: What are you letting go? Wind asks: What are you calling in? Earth asks you to ground together. Each spirit is accompanied with an acoustic element that helps your message reach the cosmos.

name: The Art of Becoming
subtitle: JacJac
description: Our hands are the spark of creativity.  They also connect us to others, our outside world, the infinite universe, and the cosmos.  We, as individuals, are connected to so much more around us, and as a collective we make up a greater whole and a greater community.  Our mini, magical dioramas will be able to be viewed via peepholes hidden amongst the tree roots of the Man Pavilion.

name: Photographs From Black Rock City 2000 to Present
subtitle: Geoffrey Squier Silver
description: A wall of Burning Man photographs, exhibited at the ARTery

name: Fireside Circle
subtitle: DA
hometown: Black Rock City, NV, NV, United States
description:
Welcome to The Fireside Circle! An ancient yet simple fire pit to gather around, to sit and tell stories with your new best friends that you haven't met yet, and get warm on the open playa. 

The firewood is set and ready for you to tend the fire.
 
Remember to keep the Black Rock Desert clean and beautiful. 

Leave No Trace.

name: MinMax Curved Benches
subtitle: MichaelWhite000
description: MinMax Curved Benches - come have a seat!  As you approach the Man or as you are leaving, have a seat and enjoy the view. Have a conversation with a new or old friend. Relax for a minute before the rest of your amazing day!

name: String Me Along
subtitle: Hatlen Art (Destiny & Drew)
hometown: The Oregon Coast, OR & Portland, OR
description: Packed into a small footprint, String Me Along has the ability to have a large impact. From a distance, colors and patterns stimulate their eyes. As they get closer, they see more of the color and even more detail in the pattern. As if begging them to play, they spin String Me Along using the crystal doorknobs and watch the interplay of color, patterns, and movement. Watching the large artwork spin draws more attention, inviting even more to play.

name: A Path thru ( to Now)
subtitle: Carmel Snow
description: A Path Thru presents two large-scale 3D knitted paintings that transform industrial knitting into mystic topographical ikat spirit maps. Developed with Innoknit atelier in Paris using engineered 3D knitting (mostly regenerative yarns), technically and graphically programmed fabric create abstract terrains inspired by paths, camouflage, maps, feelings, and the journey overall. The installation explores navigation as a living process, suggesting that pathways emerge through making, adaptation, openness, and connection, and committing to the creation on the road.

name: Mushrooms of Sirsasana
subtitle: Fonda Tong, Srikanth Guttikonda, and Looking Up Arts
description:
"Mushrooms of Sirsasana" is an installation of hand-sculpted, cast fungi inspired by wild shelf species such as turkey tail, king oyster, chicken-of-the-woods, and red belt bracket. Originally created as part of a 2022 upside-down tree sculpture in BRC, these vibrant pieces are cast in durable polyurethane resin using silicone molds. 

These mushrooms carry forward the themes of shifting perspective and cyclical rebirth. Placed within the Pavilion's Axis Mundi, they represent the living, connective tissue of the cosmic tree. While the Axis Mundi connects heaven and earth, fungi connect decay to new life.

name: What the Eyes Cannot See, the Soul Remembers
subtitle: Adrian Arias
description:
What the Eyes Cannot See, the Soul Remembers

Two canvas installations at one of the entrances to the Man Pavilion at Burning Man 2026.

The work explores the idea of invisible songs, ancestral memory, and the connection between the seen and unseen worlds. It invites us to imagine what exists beyond what the eyes can perceive—memories, sounds, spirits, and ancestral knowledge that continue to live within us.

name: ARI
subtitle: Lefty OUT There
description:
"Ari" explores the journey between birth and death, two moments we experience alone. Between them is life, shaped by the people, places, and experiences that connect us.

Inspired by the 2026 theme, Axis Mundi, the tunnel acts as a passage between these points. As participants move through its changing scale and repeating patterns, individual paths overlap within a shared structure. The pattern represents the invisible connections between us and how our lives influence one another.

Each person enters and exits alone, but the space between is experienced together. The work reflects a simple idea: our beginnings and endings may be solitary, but everything in between is interconnected.
